stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a new framework for robot policies that significantly scales visuomotor context.
Achieves an unprecedented context length of 8K timesteps without increasing inference latency.
Enables advanced capabilities like one-shot imitation learning and on-the-fly policy improvement in robotics.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a new framework for robot policies that significantly scales visuomotor context to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a major technical hurdle overcome.
Unlocks advanced capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robotics.

stories.title: First atmosphere found on Earth-like planet in habitable zone of distant star
stories.author: neversaydie
bullet_points: Discovery of the first atmosphere on an Earth-like exoplanet.
The planet is located within the habitable zone of its distant star.
This represents a major step forward in exoplanetary science and astrobiology.

stories.title: Experiments with On-device AI — What building on Gemini Nano actually teaches you
stories.author: mohanvenkatakrishnan
bullet_points: Chrome is integrating a real Large Language Model (LLM) directly into the browser.
The specific model being utilized for these on-device experiments is Gemini Nano.
The article focuses on the learning outcomes derived from building applications using this on-device AI capability.

This indicates active community interest in Meta's latest Llama model architecture.

The associated tags (transformers, safetensors) point to its implementation within the modern ML ecosystem.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: DeepSeek-V4-Pro is a trending model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and multi-token prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updates result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support with Ollama, a popular local LLM runner.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration leverages MLX, Apple's native machine learning framework, specifically for Apple Silicon.
This represents a significant step toward faster and more efficient local AI inference on Apple hardware.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Over half a million power tool batteries have been recalled due to a USB-C charging fire risk
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Greenworks Tools has initiated a massive recall affecting over half a million Kobalt-branded power tool batteries.
The recall is due to a serious fire hazard risk associated with the batteries.
Reports indicate the batteries have been observed producing smoke, sparking, or catching fire during use or charging.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The regulatory action targets apps that use manipulative design patterns to influence user behavior.
The enforcement action suggests potential revenue losses of millions for Google and Apple related to these apps.

stories.title: SpaceX scrubs Starship launch after some of its engines didn't start
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX postponed the Starship launch due to engine ignition failures.
The delay is attributed to technical issues with some of the rocket's engines.
The company plans to attempt another launch in the coming days after offloading propellant.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The paper demonstrates that pretraining data for Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned to introduce harmful behaviors.
The attack vector extends beyond limited, established data sources (like Wikipedia) to the large-scale, heterogeneous corpora used in modern LLM training.
The research highlights the critical, yet often overlooked, interaction between poisoned data and the data curation pipelines.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: Introduces SceneBind, an omni-modal representation designed to integrate vision, audio, and language for scene understanding.
Addresses a key limitation in current models by explicitly incorporating 3D spatial structure alongside instance-level semantics.
Represents scenes as semantic-spatial entities, combining global semantic embeddings with object-centric slots.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the critical bottleneck of manual and difficult-to-scale quantitative evidence synthesis in scientific fields.
The system autonomously handles the entire process from natural language question formulation to literature screening and data extraction.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical gap: linguistic safety in LLMs does not guarantee physical safety when models control embodied agents.
The study differentiates between 'content danger' (text-level risk) and 'physical danger' (real-world risk) within LLM representations.
Findings indicate that these two types of danger form separable signals in LLM architectures (tested on Qwen2.5 models).

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning introduces harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The attack feasibility extends beyond limited, established data sources to the large-scale, heterogeneous corpora typical of modern LLM training.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM deployment by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval features.

stories.title: Apple’s plot to crush OpenAI
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: Apple has initiated a lawsuit against OpenAI.
The lawsuit contains intense allegations, though experts suggest some practices may be standard industry procedure.
The article aims to analyze Apple's motivations for publicly challenging OpenAI.

stories.title: Samsung’s redesigned Z Fold 8 with a wide display just leaked
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Leaked images suggest the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 will feature a shorter, wider design.
The leak, provided by Evan Blass, predates the official July 22nd announcement event.
The leaked visuals also hint at specific hardware specifications, including a Qualcomm chipset.

stories.title: Even Microsoft couldn’t make Windows 11 work well on 8GB of RAM
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: The article discusses performance issues with Windows 11 on lower RAM configurations (specifically 8GB).
It focuses on a specific hardware product, the Microsoft Surface Laptop, highlighting a change in its usability.
The narrative suggests that software demands (Windows 11) are outpacing the capabilities of entry-level hardware.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific diagrams (schematics, plots, captions, etc.).

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new evaluation metric for AI security agents that incorporates computational cost alongside success rate.
Current security evaluations often overlook the operational cost (inference budget) of reasoning steps and tool calls in real-world scenarios.
The research tests these cost-aware evaluations on offensive Cybench challenges and defensive Splunk BOTS v1.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking capabilities.
Addresses a key limitation in current LLM agents: struggling to track task progress and getting stuck in repetitive search loops.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of open-domain information retrieval when search attempts fail.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving data.
Addresses the limitation of observational traffic data by enabling answers to 'what-if' causal questions (e.g., impact of rain).
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Tokenizers in pre-trained LLMs are often fixed based on initial training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The impact of vocabulary size on resource consumption differs significantly between large cloud models and compact models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies a core trade-off between maintaining long-horizon memory and meeting strict computational limits.
Proposes a solution to bypass the high computational cost of gradient-based memory updates required by standard Test-Time Training (TTT).

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Proposes 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences efficiently.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates upon new ratings, theoretically tightening prediction error.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in pre-trained LLMs where fixed tokenizers lead to inefficient tokenization for newly added languages.
This inefficiency manifests as increased latency, compute, and energy consumption for users of underrepresented languages.
The proposed 'In-Place Tokenizer Expansion' aims to dynamically adapt the vocabulary to better support evolving language priorities, especially for compact models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous, layer-by-layer processing.
Employs asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of physically shared neurons.
Aims to achieve computation without relying on the standard backpropagation algorithm.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a new approach for embodied control that links action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently provides robustness and safety.
BadWAM is a framework designed to model and evaluate the failure modes of these predictive control systems.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: Introduces SciDiagramEdit, a system designed to automate the editing of scientific diagrams.
The system allows authors to modify figures (relabeling, rearranging, restyling) using natural language instructions.
Addresses the complexity of scientific figures, which are dense infographics composed of heterogeneous visual elements.

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval system evaluation (static usefulness) fails when LLMs act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a document in agentic search depends on its potential to enable future actions, not just answering the current query.
The research highlights a gap between static document relevance and dynamic, causal utility in complex AI workflows.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses GI endoscopy case studies to evaluate nine existing systems, highlighting the gap between strong performance and faithful clinical reasoning.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves challenge performance, it doesn't guarantee complete or trustworthy clinical explanations.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically for stance analysis on TikTok.
Addresses the gap in computational analysis for short-video political discourse by integrating audiovisual and conversational data.
The dataset is focused on the 2024 U.S. election cycle, covering political discussions involving major figures.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource usage.
The impact of this inefficiency is more pronounced in compact models compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Identifies a limitation in existing methods: they approximate log-likelihood by ignoring the sequential nature of unmasking during generation.
Proposes a novel approach, 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients,' to better model the two decision points (token placement and masking) at each generation step.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on LLM usage in kernel development
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds, a key figure in Linux development, is discussing the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into kernel development.
The topic addresses the practical application and implications of AI tools within the core infrastructure of operating systems.
This represents a moderate but significant discussion point regarding the future tooling and development practices in low-level systems programming.

stories.title: PACT: Anonymous Credentials for the Web – Mozilla Hacks
stories.author: hacks.mozilla.org via brn
bullet_points: The article discusses PACT, a project focused on enabling anonymous credentials for the web.
This relates to privacy-enhancing technologies and decentralized web infrastructure.
It is presented as a technical deep-dive from Mozilla Hacks, suggesting a moderate level of technical depth.

stories.title: My Inferentia port matched its reference token-for-token — and still output garbage
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details a complex engineering challenge: porting a large language model (Gemma-4 31B) to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
The standard tensor-parallel scaling recipe that worked for smaller models failed when scaled to 31B parameters.
The author highlights a critical issue where a successful validation check can mask underlying, severe performance degradation ('output garbage').

stories.title: Porting a 128-expert MoE (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2 — where every rank weighted the wrong experts
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the complex engineering challenge of porting a large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model (Gemma-4 26B-A4B) to AWS Inferentia2.
Key technical hurdles included implementing a dual-path Feed-Forward Network (FFN) and managing a sparse expert loop that failed to trace correctly.
The team encountered a difficult debugging issue where the device output was empty despite perfect CPU reference results and passing unit tests.

stories.title: Porting Gemma-4 12B (the encoder-free multimodal one) to AWS Inferentia2
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the process of porting the Gemma-4 12B multimodal model to AWS Inferentia2 hardware.
A key technical challenge encountered was the sliding-window attention overflowing Neuron's fused-attention SBUF.
After applying three fixes, the model achieved a throughput of approximately 15 tokens/second on a single inf2.8xlarge instance.

stories.title: Five Gemma-4 models, one accelerator: what porting E2B 31B to AWS Inferentia2 taught me
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article details the performance comparison of five different Gemma-4 model variants on AWS Inferentia2.
It explores various optimization techniques used, including PLE, KV-sharing, MatFormer, mixed attention, and MoE.
The author shares insights gained from the porting process, including a recurring bug encountered across all tested models.
